strings.name: Liang Mong-song
strings.summary: Liang Mong-song is a Taiwan-born semiconductor engineer who worked at TSMC and Samsung before joining SMIC as co-CEO in 2017. His career focuses on memory, advanced logic processes and technical team management. Process achievements depend on research, manufacturing and supply-chain collaboration.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Departure from the board is distinct from service as co-CEO; development, production and process-node labels are not interchangeable. Historical civil restrictions are not described as criminal convictions.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to advanced semiconductor process research and technology management, influencing wafer fabrication and Asia’s chip industry.
strings.facts.f1.label: Doctoral research
strings.facts.f1.value: Berkeley PhD in 1984 under Chenming Hu; thesis examined degradation of thin gate-oxide MOSFETs under current and electric-field stress.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current and former offices
strings.facts.f2.value: The 2026 interim report still lists him as co-CEO. Executive director from October 16, 2017 to November 11, 2021; leaving the board did not end the co-CEO role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Process research and team management
strings.highlights.h1.text: Works on memory and advanced logic manufacturing processes, connecting device research, integration and manufacturing. Company-wide breakthroughs are not attributed solely to him.
strings.highlights.h2.title: 14-nanometer production milestone
strings.highlights.h2.text: SMIC reports first-generation 14nm FinFET wafer revenue in Q4 2019, a company and team achievement during his tenure.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Interim report continues to list co-CEO role
strings.timeline.t1.text: Company report records his office and 2026 equity awards. Share grants are not cash salary or evidence of a personal public appearance.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Leaves board, remains co-CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: Annual report confirms the executive directorship ended while co-CEO duties continued; he did not thereby leave SMIC.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Company brings 14nm process into production
strings.timeline.t3.text: First-generation FinFET contributed about 1% of Q4 wafer revenue, not total annual revenue or proof of production at more advanced nodes.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joins SMIC as co-CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: Appointed alongside Zhao Haijun and also becomes executive director. Board chairman is a separate office.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Final ruling in TSMC employment dispute
strings.timeline.t5.text: Legal commentary and reporting describe the Supreme Court upholding restrictions on serving Samsung through the end of 2015. A historical civil restriction, not a criminal conviction or current ban.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Samsung Electronics
strings.timeline.t6.text: Enters semiconductor technology work at Samsung after teaching in South Korea; the later TSMC dispute is recorded separately.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leaves TSMC
strings.timeline.t7.text: Ends about 17 years with the company, including advanced-process research. Departure motives and unverified salary rumors are not inferred.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes Berkeley doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: University thesis record and advisor’s alumni list both give 1984, with research on thin gate-oxide MOSFET reliability.
